title: Sensor device abstraction with fake sensor

parent.objective: Bring up a host-side bridge for the fictional SYNTH-SENSOR-1 so that every component is verified independently and no hardware behavior is claimed before it is observed.
parent.milestone: Device sequencing verified against a fake sensor

goal: Implement request/reply sequencing for one sensor over any Transport, with a scripted fake sensor as its test double.
non_goals: Communicate with, or claim behavior of, any physical device.

prohibited: Edit codec, transport, adapter or telemetry modules.
Treat a fake-sensor pass as device compatibility.

inputs.name: Read sequence
inputs.description: Send encode_read_request(); receive one frame; decode_reading; errors become DeviceError.

inputs.name: Fake sensor script
inputs.description: Scripted readings with optional checksum corruption every N replies.

outputs.name: Device module
outputs.description: SensorDevice.read() returning a Reading or raising DeviceError.

outputs.name: Fake sensor
outputs.description: FakeSensorTransport answering read requests from a script.

interface.name: synth_bridge.device
interface.description: SensorDevice(transport, timeout_s).read() -> Reading; DeviceError names the codec error code.

assumptions: The fake sensor is a simulator; it encodes the specification's expectations, not observed behavior.

sources.authority: Synthetic specification invented for this example; not a manufacturer document.

sources.reference: examples/software-hardware/sample — the synthetic bridge package and its tests
sources.authority: Reference implementation for this example only; establishes no real device behavior.

acceptance_criteria.description: Scripted readings are returned in order through the fake sensor.
Silence surfaces as no reply and a corrupted reply names the codec error code.
A loopback echo is rejected as BAD_PAYLOAD, never accepted as a reading.

validation.description: Run the device tests against the fake sensor and loopback.

context_scope: Interfaces of synth_bridge.codec and synth_bridge.transport only.
architecture_boundaries: Request/reply sequencing lives only in device.py.
Do not change the codec or transport interfaces.

hardware_assumptions.assumption: A physical SYNTH-SENSOR-1 answers each read request with exactly one reply frame or stays silent.
